components.gap: Lyndon 1959 (Pacific J. Math. 9, pp. 143-154) is reproduced in full mathematically (Propositions 1-3, Theorem 4, Corollaries 4.1-4.2, Theorem 5 with its three cases, Corollaries 5.1-5.3, the two-system strengthening, Theorem 5' with the torsion-free example, and the three complementary examples), but these source claims are absent from presentations/n-a-011-02.tex and its annex: (1) p. 143: the easy direction is called not difficult, while the converse, though nearly as obvious intuitively, appears to be a matter of considerable difficulty (lines 11-17 report only the priority attributions); (2) p. 143: Los's announced but unpublished proof used methods quite different from Lyndon's, and Mal'cev stated the result and only appears to indicate a method of proof (lines 14-15 drop the different-methods claim and the hedge); (3) p. 144 and footnote 1: the paper is placed within Tarski's theory of elementary classes [12, 13], with 'elementary class' meaning Tarski's arithmetical class in the wider sense (AC_Delta), and the concept of elementary extension is credited to Tarski and Vaught [15]; (4) p. 146 footnote 4: Q-maps and elementary extension are special cases of Keisler's more far-reaching ideas [4]; the constants w_a derive from A. Robinson's diagrams [11]; and Proposition 3 is contained in Th. 1.11 of Tarski-Vaught [15]. The handbook instead titles the construction 'Lyndon's expanded diagram' (lines 123-136) with no priority note; (5) p. 153 footnotes 5-7: the paragraph's concepts of theory and undecidability are referred to Tarski-Mostowski-Robinson [14]; the undecidability of the pure predicate example to Church [1]; and that of elementary group theory to [14, p. 84] and Tarski's reference there, see also Novikov [10]. Lines 329-332 and annex lines 441-444 call these an unnamed external premise; (6) p. 144: the acknowledgement of discussions with Henkin and Tarski, and footnote 3's occasion of Robinson's suggestion (AMS Summer Institute, Ithaca, 1957). Write these claims, attributed to the source, into the section's opening (lines 11-17), the diagram/Proposition 3 material (lines 123-136) and the undecidability theorem (lines 324-333).

components.notes: Whole extent pp. 143-154 compared item by item against the held publisher PDF. Mathematical statements, cases, examples, the auxiliary-identity/function/falsum conventions, the Q-map, positivity and relative arguments and the explicit interpolation dependency are all present. The gaps are omitted historical, attributive and justificatory claims only.

components.notes: Written proofs at annex lines 11-294 cover every step of sections 2-4 (Proposition 1 induction; Proposition 2 by compactness and the imported polarity interpolation theorem; map/kernel/quotient lemma; Proposition 3; Theorem 4 both directions, including removal of diagram constants and the pull-back for non-injective maps; Corollaries 4.1-4.2; Theorem 5 in all three cases with quotients by e; Corollaries 5.1-5.3; the two-system proposition; Theorem 5' and the relative corollaries). Operations, constants, freely interpreted e with later quotienting, 0/1, and H-relative consequence are all kept. The one external dependency is the polarity interpolation theorem, which the source itself imports from [7]. N-a-011-C01 frames it as an explicit dependency, so it does not have to be proved here.

source_locators.item: positive sentence = conjunction, disjunction, quantification, no negation; preservation under homomorphic images
homomorphism = R-map, a map onto (all Q-maps are onto, p. 146)

components.notes: The source treats only onto maps. The comparison pairs existential-positive formulas with arbitrary homomorphisms and positive formulas (with universal quantifiers) with onto homomorphisms, and says 'onto' cannot be replaced by 'arbitrary' (lines 336-339). Host lines 214-217 and 259-263 add that positive is not existential-positive and that the arbitrary-homomorphism pairing is a distinct theorem. The separating counterexample is the sentence 'for all x, P(x)' under a non-onto inclusion (lines 345-347). It is verified at annex lines 450-457, which also prove the arbitrary-homomorphism preservation direction.

source_locators.item: Corollaries 5.1-5.3 over all relational systems of elementary classes
first complementary example: K = all finite systems, H(K) contained in K, conclusion of Theorem 5 fails

components.notes: The all-structures regime is stated at host lines 182-183, presentation lines 200-201 and 339-340. The reason finite-only variants cannot substitute is given at lines 350-351 and annex lines 471-474: the compactness constructions produce arbitrary infinite extensions, and neither hypotheses nor conclusions impose finiteness. Host lines 303-305 add a finite failure of the Los-Tarski substructure form. The finite-sets example (lines 240-245, annex lines 313-332) shows the conclusion failing for a finite-only class.

summary: MAP-03, MAP-04, MAP-05 and MAP-06 are covered on the route. N-a-011-C01 is partial: the complete Lyndon 1959 presentation omits several of the source's historical, attributive and justificatory claims (pp. 143, 144, 146 n. 4, 153 nn. 5-7).
